sentences.text:
The Hon'Ble Smt.Justice Tirumala Devi Eada
 Criminal Petition No.11176 of 2025
Order:

-
1. This Criminal Petition is filed under Section 528 of Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS),
2023 seeking to quash the proceedings against the petitioner/accused No.4 in C.C.No.8085 of 2020,
on the file of the learned XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad,
registered for the offences under Sections 406 and 420 read with 34 of IPC.

entities.text: XII Additional Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Nampally, Hyderabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Heard Dr.J.Viplav Babu, learned counsel for the petitioner/accused No.4 as well as Sri Jitender Rao Veeramalla, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing for the respondent No.1-State.
3.

Though notice was sent to the 2nd respondent to the address mentioned in the charge sheet, the same was returned with an endorsement "Addressee not known" on one occasion and "addressee left" on another occasion.
Hence, it is held to be a deemed service.

4. Learned counsel for the petitioner has submitted that the petitioner is a student and due to his poor economical condition, he used to work as an office boy under accused Nos.1 to 3 and ETD,J Crl.P.No.11176_2025 according to their instructions, he used to supply the material.

Except for that,
he is not at all concerned with any other allegations in the case.
He further submitted that the petitioner has completed his Graduation and is pursuing MBA.
Due to continuation of proceedings against the petitioner, his career is at stake.
He therefore prayed to quash the proceedings against the petitioner.

5. The learned Additional Public Prosecutor has submitted that the averment against the petitioner is that accused No.4, being the employee of accused Nos.1 to 3, also used to collect amounts from the retailers from time to time regularly.
He therefore prayed to pass appropriate orders.
6. Perused the record.

The recitals of charge sheet point out that accused No.4 was an employee of accused Nos.1 to 3 and the only allegation against the petitioner is that he used to collect amounts from the retailers regularly.
Except for that, there is no allegation in the charge sheet.

Considering the averments in the charge sheet and also the submissions of both the counsel, accused No.4 is said to be an office boy under accused Nos.1 to 3 and that as part of his duties entrusted by accused Nos.1 to 3, he used to collect money from the retailers.

The said act does not attract the ingredients ETD,J Crl.P.No.11176_2025 under Section 420 of IPC and therefore, the continuation of proceedings against the petitioner would be abuse of process of law.
